clue.text: Cluedo. Mortal sin. I will be outstanding suspect!

definitions.text: Cluedo. Mortal sin. I will be outstanding suspect!

indicators.note: something suspect is dodgy and not to be trusted as given, so the letters are rearranged
read as 'out-standing', the letter is to stand outside, so it is dropped from the string

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: A Cluedo player, sure of the killer, accuses a suspect of the deadly sin of murder.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the I from CLUEDO MORTAL SIN and rearrange the fourteen letters left. The whole clue doubles as the definition: one of the six suspects in the board game Cluedo (Clue in North America).
explanation.definitionFit: Colonel Mustard is one of the six murder suspects in the classic detective board game, alongside Miss Scarlett and Professor Plum.

clue.text: Corgi a stick's helping to make frenzied

indicators.note: a helping is a portion, so the answer is a portion of the words around it

parts.note: the letters run across these words, minus the first and last two

explanation.surface: A dog with a stick in its mouth gets wildly excited.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgiastic behaviour is wild and unrestrained, like a riotous revel, which is close to frenzied excitement.

clue.text: Tipsy — oldies almost sozzled!

indicators.note: sozzled means very drunk, and a drunk's letters stagger into a new order
almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A tipsy bunch of pensioners, nearly blind drunk at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled is informal slang for drunk, as in well-oiled, so it matches someone slightly merry from drink.

clue.text: Parts of roof fall away, exposing a snoop

parts.note: the overhanging lower edges of a roof
to drop is to fall away

explanation.surface: Pieces of a roof tumble off and reveal someone spying from above.
explanation.definitionFit: To eavesdrop is to listen secretly to others' private conversations, which is a way to pry or snoop.

clue.text: Month on topless resort somewhere in the Med

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, so the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: M is a standard abbreviation for month
Yalta is a Black Sea resort in Crimea

explanation.surface: A month spent at a topless beach resort somewhere on the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless resort' suggests a nudist beach, but it is Yalta losing its first letter. In a down clue, 'on' puts M above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is an island nation in the central Mediterranean Sea, south of Sicily, so it is one place in the Med.

clue.text: Ill-frequented locale where forbidden sauce is stuffed into fish

indicators.note: stuffing puts something inside, so the first words go within the last word

parts.note: a flatfish
something ruled out is not allowed
HP Sauce is a well-known British brown sauce

explanation.surface: A dodgy place where a banned sauce gets crammed inside a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: HP is a brand of brown sauce found on British tables. 'Ill-frequented' means rarely visited, not frequented by bad people.
explanation.definitionFit: The southernmost point on Earth sits in remote Antarctica and receives very few visitors, so it is a seldom-visited spot.

clue.text: Comrade Lenin provides cover for artist

indicators.note: the outer words cover the answer, which sits concealed inside them

parts.note: found spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A Soviet revolutionary shelters a painter from the authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is a Grammy-winning English singer-songwriter, and recording performers are commonly called artists in the music business.

clue.text: Deserted soul singer, not given intro, panics

indicators.note: without an introduction the name loses its opening letter

parts.note: d. is a dictionary abbreviation for deserted
Bill Withers, the American soul singer of Ain't No Sunshine

explanation.surface: An abandoned soul singer, denied an introduction on stage, falls into a panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dithers is flustered and indecisive, and in British use being in a dither means being agitated or panicky.

clue.text: Fashions displayed by quiet monkeys

parts.note: the word you say to call for quiet
primates, loosely monkeys

explanation.surface: Clothes modelled on a catwalk by silent monkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashions' looks like a plural noun for clothes; here it is a verb meaning forms or moulds.
explanation.definitionFit: To shape something is to form or mould it, which is the verb sense of fashion, as in fashioning a pot from clay.

clue.text: Tip describes good philosopher

indicators.note: to describe can mean to draw a line around, so one word encircles the other

parts.note: a ship that heels tips to one side
G is a standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A useful piece of advice explains what makes a good thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' reads as a hint, but it is the verb, to lean over, and 'describes' in its geometric sense of drawing round.
explanation.definitionFit: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel was the German idealist thinker known for his dialectic, a major figure of nineteenth-century philosophy.

clue.text: Pastry: victual cooked with oven (wanting no internal combustion?)

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed into something new
wanting no means lacking, so those letters are taken out of the mix

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
IC is the abbreviation for internal combustion, as in IC engine

explanation.surface: A recipe note: bake the food in an oven, not over a combustion engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A vol-au-vent is a small hollow case of puff pastry, usually filled with a savoury mixture and served as a canape.

clue.text: Manners princes, queens curtly display

parts.note: P abbreviates prince; curtly asks for the short forms, here plural
the comma in a list stands for and
Q abbreviates queen, here plural

explanation.surface: Royals show off their good etiquette, if a little brusquely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtly' looks like it describes rude royals, but it tells you to shorten the two words to their abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Minding your Ps and Qs is an idiom for being polite and careful about etiquette, so the phrase stands for good behaviour.

clue.text: Competitor permitted to enter re-staged heat

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one word sits within the other
something re-staged is put on in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A runner is allowed into a heat that has to be rerun.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete takes part in sporting events such as races and field events, so is a contestant or competitor.

clue.text: Begin to incriminate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to establish or start something, such as a business
second meaning: to frame someone so they look guilty

explanation.surface: An instruction to start framing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to found or start something and to frame an innocent person with planted evidence.

clue.text: Hairy figure to dismiss two batsmen, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the phrase is said with its initial sounds exchanged

parts.note: in cricket, to dismiss two batsmen is to bowl a pair; swap the opening sounds

explanation.surface: A cricketer with a big beard takes two wickets.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler dismisses batsmen; 'bowl a pair' with B and P exchanged sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The large Arctic bear has a thick shaggy coat of white fur, so it is a very furry creature, playfully called a figure.

clue.text: Conservatives pursue fun in ecclesiastical dwellings

indicators.note: to pursue is to follow behind, so the first word comes after the second

parts.note: short for recreation
Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Tory politicians chase after a good time in church houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectory is the house provided for a parish rector, a clergyman, so these are church residences.

clue.text: A neurotic ordered strong liquor

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so these letters are sorted afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An anxious person asks for a stiff drink at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange-flavoured liqueur of about forty per cent alcohol, so it is a potent spirit.

clue.text: Wanting kiss, exhilarant, worked up and rabid

indicators.note: something worked up is stirred about, so the letters are mixed
wanting means lacking, so the named letter must be missing

parts.note: X is the kiss at the end of a letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Without a kiss, someone thrilled becomes agitated and furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a lather is an idiom for being agitated or very angry, like a sweating horse, matching frenzied fury.

clue.text: Typical! EU corrupted by oil suppliers

indicators.note: corrupted means spoiled or altered from its proper form, so the letters change order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble that, as usual, Brussels has been bribed by oil companies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil suppliers' suggests petroleum firms; eucalyptus trees yield eucalyptus oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalypts are gum trees whose leaves are distilled to produce aromatic eucalyptus oil, so the trees provide that oil.

clue.text: The Spanish bubbly (cava, primarily) is reminiscent of rubber

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: A Spanish sparkling wine, mainly cava, that tastes like rubber.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic stretches and springs back into shape, the defining property of rubber, so it resembles that material.

clue.text: Bang on, demand and obtain

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to insist on and get, as in a payment or revenge

explanation.surface: Spot on: insist on something and get it.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means precisely accurate; as a verb it means to insist on and extract, as with exacting revenge.

clue.text: Not dead drunk, embracing one in orderly fashion

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in your arms, so one piece goes inside the other
not means without, so the letter for the first word is removed

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk
D is a standard abbreviation for dead
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone only merry rather than paralytic hugs a friend neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiddly is British slang for a little drunk; one of its two Ds goes, then I is put in.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidily is the adverb from tidy, meaning neatly and in an orderly way, so it describes doing things in order.

clue.text: Broadcast to omit sudden lowering of food supplies

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
to drop is to leave out

explanation.surface: A TV channel cuts a programme because of falling food stocks.
explanation.definitionFit: An airdrop delivers aid supplies by parachute from an aircraft, a descent of food and equipment from the sky.

clue.text: Renovate Magritte, perhaps, with tip of hacksaw

parts.note: Rene Magritte, the Belgian surrealist painter; perhaps flags an example of the name

indicators.note: the tip of a saw is its far end, so only the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: Restoring a Magritte painting with a hacksaw, which seems unwise.
explanation.walkthrough: The tip of a hacksaw could be either end; here it is the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew something is to restore it to a fresh condition, and renovating likewise means repairing and refreshing.

clue.text: Unhealthy-looking pie

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pale and sickly in complexion
second meaning: a folded pastry case with a savoury filling, as in a Cornish one

explanation.surface: A pie that looks bad for your health.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means pallid and sickly; as a noun it is a pastry turnover filled with meat and vegetables.

clue.text: Creator of effigies leaving EU bigwig and Arabian unfinished

indicators.note: unfinished means lacking its end, so each word loses its final letter

parts.note: Donald Tusk, former President of the European Council
a Saudi is an Arabian from Saudi Arabia

explanation.surface: A sculptor quits Brussels, leaving behind an EU leader and an Arab, both half done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving EU' suggests Brexit or removing the letters EU, but EU belongs with the bigwig, Donald Tusk.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie Tussaud was the wax sculptor who founded Madame Tussauds, the London museum of lifelike wax figures of famous people.

clue.text: Got a whiff of fish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: past tense of smell, in British spelling
second meaning: a small silvery food fish

explanation.surface: Someone caught the smell of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The British past tense of the verb meaning to sense an odour, and also the name of a small edible silvery fish.

clue.text: Teens seen around Elvis' home

indicators.note: around suggests letters moved about and scattered, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Young fans spotted near Graceland, Elvis Presley's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like it means near the house, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley lived at Graceland in Memphis, so the US state containing that city was where the singer made his home.

clue.text: Source of alcohol the drunken yokel emptied

indicators.note: a drunken person reels about, so these letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its contents, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Where the boozy country bumpkin got his drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethyl alcohol is ethanol, the kind found in drinks, and the ethyl group is the chemical radical from which it is formed.

clue.text: Chicken? Playwright has yen to get a bit of pudding

parts.note: Noel Coward, the English playwright
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency
custard is a dessert sauce often poured on pudding

explanation.surface: A dramatist craves a spoonful of dessert, perhaps with chicken on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pudding also means dessert generally; custard is a sweet sauce served with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowardy custard is a British childish taunt for a timid person, and chicken is slang for exactly such a coward.
